answer: Each new key must evaluate a Wesolowski VDF for 4 sequential hours before admission, and the proof binds to the pubkey. Every epoch a beacon pulse seeds a cipher puzzle, and a random 32-agent cohort must threshold-decrypt it, 22 signatures required, so a fresh key is audited by strangers. For 10,000 fakes, an attacker burns 40,000 core-hours, about $2,000 at $0.05, and needs 10,000 parallel cores to finish in 4 hours. Capturing 22 of 32 seats needs control of most of the network. Identities accrete the way coral builds a reef, slow and layered, and a forger pays for every ledge.
